clue.text: Exclude man with a head scarf

explanation.surface: Someone shuts out a man who is wearing a scarf on his head.
explanation.walkthrough: Crossword setters often use 'man' to stand for any short male name; here it is DAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandana is a large coloured kerchief tied around the head or neck.

clue.text: Piece of feathery material on top of the Queen's hats

indicators.note: in a down entry, on means placed above what follows

parts.note: a feather boa is a long fluffy scarf

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down answer is its first letter

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, with the possessive S

explanation.surface: A feather trim placed atop Her Majesty's hats.
explanation.walkthrough: A boater is a flat-topped straw hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Boaters are stiff straw hats with flat crowns, once worn for boating.

clue.text: Heroin bug destroyed the man just up the road

definitions.text: the man just up the road

indicators.note: something destroyed is broken up, so the letters are reassembled differently

explanation.surface: Drugs and a virus ruined the man who lives down the street.
explanation.definitionFit: A neighbour is someone living nearby, such as a person a few doors along the street.

clue.text: Parting remark from a daughter that is universal

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
U is the film certificate for universal

explanation.surface: A daughter says a goodbye that everyone recognises.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film rating meaning suitable for all audiences.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is a French farewell used in English, a remark made on parting.

clue.text: Positions of tents initially situated all over the place

indicators.note: scattered everywhere, so the letters are jumbled
initially points to the first letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Tents pitched haphazardly across a campsite.
explanation.definitionFit: Attitudes are postures or stances, the ways a body or opinion is placed.

clue.text: It is found in skull contents here

indicators.note: something found in another thing sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

explanation.surface: A puzzle about what exactly lies inside the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Here' as a definition is the setter's home country: the Guardian is a British paper, so 'here' is where its solvers are.
explanation.definitionFit: From the British setter's point of view, the country where the crossword is printed is simply 'here'.

clue.text: Some grab ready money

indicators.note: some of the following words means only part of their letters are used

explanation.surface: A thief snatches some cash on hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready money' reads as one phrase for cash, but 'ready' is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread is old slang for money.

clue.text: Bury reported panic and poke your nose in

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so we go by how it is said

explanation.surface: Panic spreads in a town and someone meddles.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury is also a town near Manchester, which pulls the surface reading away from burial.
explanation.definitionFit: To interfere is to meddle in others' affairs, which is the idiom 'poke your nose in'.

clue.text: Skilled in one small area of work

explanation.surface: Someone is expert in a narrow field of employment.
explanation.definitionFit: Adept means highly proficient or expert at something.

clue.text: Unpretentious old city in former South African province

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it

parts.note: the province merged into KwaZulu-Natal in 1994

explanation.surface: A modest ancient city lay in a now-defunct South African region.
explanation.walkthrough: Ur is the crossword's favourite old city, in ancient Mesopotamia.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural manner is unaffected and genuine, without airs.

clue.text: I bail out with an excuse

indicators.note: 'out' suggests things knocked out of place, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A prisoner says they paid bail to get out and offers a reason.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a claim of having been elsewhere, used as an excuse or defence.

clue.text: Drugs possibly cure people at first sign of tuberculosis

parts.note: to cure an illness is to treat it

indicators.note: the first sign of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the disease

explanation.surface: A medical note about curing patients once tuberculosis first shows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' marks drugs as just one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Medication is one kind of medical treatment, so drugs are an example of it.

clue.text: Burnt out former girlfriend detested being without us

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: 'without' in its old sense of 'outside' means one piece wraps round the other

explanation.surface: An ex-girlfriend who loathed the couple is described as burnt out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but here it has its old sense of outside, as in the hymn line 'a green hill far away, without a city wall'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone burnt out is utterly worn out, with all energy used up.

clue.text: It goes round both ways

parts.note: surface reading: something that can spin clockwise or anticlockwise
setter's reading: a spinning part whose name reads the same forwards and backwards

explanation.walkthrough: The machine part turns, and its five-letter name is a palindrome, so it also 'goes round' when read either way.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotor is the rotating component of a machine such as a helicopter or turbine.

clue.text: Talked in English following special approval

indicators.note: one thing following another comes after it, setting the order of the pieces

parts.note: sp. is a dictionary abbreviation for special
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Someone spoke in English once given special permission.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoke is the past tense of speak, meaning talked.

clue.text: Around here maple is short-lived

indicators.note: turned around means moved about, so the letters change places

explanation.surface: Local maple trees do not last long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' seems to mean 'in this area', but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephemeral describes something lasting only a very brief time.

clue.text: Clan held a reunion in a place of entertainment

indicators.note: a reunion brings things together again in a new gathering, so the letters regroup

explanation.surface: A Scottish clan gathers again at a local venue.
explanation.definitionFit: A dance hall is a large public room for dancing, a classic venue for a night's entertainment.

clue.text: French singer's claim made without compunction

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Edith Piaf's song 'Non, je ne regrette rien'
second meaning: describing a choice taken with no remorse

explanation.surface: A French chanteuse insists she feels no guilt.
explanation.walkthrough: Edith Piaf's famous song title translates as 'No, I regret nothing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no regrets means feeling no remorse about one's actions, which is acting without compunction.

clue.text: Gave up on a journalist covering the group live

indicators.note: a covering goes over and around what it hides

parts.note: a show that is on is live

explanation.surface: A reporter quit covering a band's live gig.
explanation.definitionFit: Abandoned means deserted or quit, having stopped persisting with something.

clue.text: Person paying has an advantage right at the start

indicators.note: the advantage is placed at the start, ahead of the other piece

parts.note: purchase can mean a grip or leverage, an advantage
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A paying customer starts with the upper hand.
explanation.walkthrough: Purchase here is not buying but a firm hold or leverage, as in 'getting purchase on a rock'.
explanation.definitionFit: A purchaser is a buyer, the one who pays for goods.

clue.text: Opted for fruit pud with a different filling

indicators.note: a different filling means the middle letter is swapped for another

parts.note: taken as written; British slang for pudding

explanation.surface: Someone chose a fruit pudding with a new filling.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle U of PUD is replaced by E, giving PED.
explanation.definitionFit: To plump for something is an idiom for choosing it decisively.

clue.text: Demand is strictly correct

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a verb, to insist on or extract payment

explanation.surface: Someone insists a demand is quite proper.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to require forcibly; as an adjective it means precise and accurate.

clue.text: I used to be terribly boring

indicators.note: terribly means badly, so the letters are messed up

explanation.surface: Someone admits they once were dreadfully dull.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is 'I used to', and 'be' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tedious means tiresome and dull, wearing out one's patience.

clue.text: Branch of international organisation to get rid of weapons

parts.note: an arm is a branch of an organisation

explanation.surface: A section of a UN agency is tasked with disarmament.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'branch of' the organisation is read as the organisation then its arm.
explanation.definitionFit: To unarm is an old form of disarm: to take weapons away.

clue.text: A drug-free European capital has a peculiar charm

indicators.note: free of something means without it, so it is taken out

explanation.surface: A clean-living capital city has a special appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: Rome loses its E, then the second 'a' completes the word.
explanation.definitionFit: An aroma is a distinctive pervasive quality, a special atmosphere or charm.

clue.text: Cocky leader interrupts important Labour politician

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something

explanation.surface: An arrogant leader cuts in on a senior Labour figure.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour is a major British political party; Ed Miliband led it from 2010 to 2015.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone bigheaded is conceited, full of self-importance.

clue.text: Be extremely restricted behind a face covering

indicators.note: behind sets the order: one piece comes after another
the extremes of a word are its two end letters

explanation.surface: Advice to keep a low profile behind a mask.
explanation.definitionFit: A beard is facial hair that covers the chin and cheeks.

clue.text: Come in from garden terrace

indicators.note: taken from the following words, so the letters lie within them

explanation.surface: An invitation to step inside off the patio.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter is to go or come into a place.

clue.text: Breed of wild copra tree

indicators.note: wild means untamed and disordered, so the letters run loose

explanation.surface: A variety of untamed coconut tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breed' looks like a noun meaning a variety, but it is the verb. Copra is dried coconut kernel.
explanation.definitionFit: To procreate is to produce offspring, the verb sense of breeding.

clue.text: Dance beat has energy

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them

explanation.surface: A dance with an energetic rhythm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat' suggests a musical rhythm, but it is the verb meaning thrash.
explanation.definitionFit: The tango is a ballroom dance from Argentina.

clue.text: Rang about help before student took charge

indicators.note: turning about means facing the other way, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: to lead is to take charge

explanation.surface: Someone phoned for help before a student took over.
explanation.definitionFit: To dial a number is to ring it on the telephone.

clue.text: Way to deliver oddly easy progress

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
to deliver from something is to rid of it

indicators.note: oddly keeps the letters in odd-numbered positions, the first, third and so on

explanation.surface: A recipe for making progress without difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deliver' in the sense of rescue or free, as in 'deliver us from evil'.
explanation.definitionFit: Strides are advances or headway, as in 'making great strides'.
